title: Radicle team
description: Contents of .radicle/team.json on the default branch of a team repository. One repository describes exactly one team. The repository's RID is the team's identifier; its delegates are the team's admins.

version.description: Schema version, not the team's version. Incremented only on breaking changes. A consumer that does not understand this value must refuse to interpret the file rather than parse it partially.

description.description: Short summary of the team. Long form content belongs in .radicle/profile/README.md.

members.description: DIDs of the team's members. Membership is a claim by whoever controls this repository and grants no access to anything.

repos.description: RIDs of the repositories associated with the team. Association is a claim and does not require the repository's consent.

did.description: The lexical form of a canonical Radicle peer identifier: did:key: followed by a 48 character base58btc value beginning z6Mk. The pattern rejects the encodings used by other standard key types, but it does not prove that the decoded multicodec is ed25519-pub; consumers must decode the value for conformance.

rid.description: A repository identifier: rad: followed by a multibase base58btc encoding (leading z) of a Git object identifier. Bounded to the SHA-1 object format, the only one Radicle defines today; a new object format will require a new bound.
